summary.text: The formal statement is simply the tautology \(\mathrm{True}\), so it holds unconditionally and no number-theoretic argument is involved.

full_proof.text:
The proposition to be proved is simply \(\mathrm{True}\).

By definition, \(\mathrm{True}\) is the proposition that holds unconditionally: it requires no hypotheses, imposes no constraints, and has its canonical proof merely by virtue of being the true proposition. Therefore \(\mathrm{True}\) holds.

This completes the proof.
